title: API Design
blurb: REST/GraphQL/gRPC design, versioning, idempotency and pagination.

quiz.question: REST resource URLs should prefer…
quiz.explanation: Resources are nouns; HTTP methods express the action.

quiz.question: Idempotent HTTP methods include…
quiz.explanation: Safe/idempotent: GET/HEAD/OPTIONS; idempotent writes: PUT/DELETE. POST is not idempotent.

quiz.question: JWT auth typically sends the token in…
quiz.explanation: Stateless REST: client sends JWT each request; server validates signature/claims.

quiz.question: Best status code for successfully creating a resource?
quiz.explanation: 201 Created (often with Location header) for successful POST create.

quiz.question: Pagination on list endpoints exists mainly to…
options: Bound response size and DB load
quiz.explanation: Never return unbounded lists in production APIs.

quiz.question: Best default for public CRUD HTTP API?
GraphQL caching is harder because…
options: Queries vary by shape; URL cache keys less natural

quiz.question: Mixed architecture pattern?
options: One giant GraphQL for DBs directly

quiz.question: Which change to a response is backward compatible?
options: Changing a type from string to integer
quiz.explanation: Additive changes are safe when clients ignore unknown fields.

quiz.question: What is application/problem+json?
quiz.explanation: It gives a consistent type/title/status/detail error shape.

quiz.question: Why does cursor (keyset) pagination beat OFFSET on large tables?
options: Each page is an index seek, and it is stable under inserts
quiz.explanation: OFFSET scans and discards rows, and items shift when new rows arrive.

quiz.question: Which response tells a client how long to wait after being rate limited?
quiz.explanation: Clients should back off using Retry-After plus jitter.

quiz.question: Why must webhook consumers deduplicate on the event id?
options: Delivery is at-least-once, so duplicates happen
quiz.explanation: Retries after timeouts redeliver the same event.

quiz.question: The best way to verify a webhook's authenticity is…
options: An HMAC of timestamp + raw body with a shared secret, compared in constant time
quiz.explanation: The signature plus a timestamp tolerance prevents tampering and replay.

problems.title: Design Order Endpoints
problems.prompt: Sketch REST endpoints for listing a user’s orders (paginated), creating an order, and canceling an order. Include status codes.
problems.solution: GET /users/{id}/orders?page=&size= → 200; POST /orders → 201 + Location; POST /orders/{id}/cancel or PATCH status → 200; missing → 404.

problems.title: Idempotency Key
problems.prompt: How would you make payment creation safe against double-submit from a flaky client?
problems.solution: Require Idempotency-Key. Persist key + response. Retries with same key return the original result without charging twice.

problems.title: Choose API style
problems.prompt: Mobile app needs many screens with different fields from same backend. Options?
problems.solution: GraphQL or a BFF that shapes REST DTOs per screen.

problems.title: Secure GraphQL
problems.prompt: List 3 production controls for a public GraphQL endpoint.
problems.solution: AuthZ per field; max depth/complexity; persisted queries; rate limits; timeout.

problems.title: Keyset pagination
problems.prompt: Implement /orders?limit=&cursor= over (created_at DESC, id DESC) with an opaque cursor.
problems.solution: Query WHERE (created_at,id) < (:c,:i) ORDER BY created_at DESC, id DESC LIMIT limit+1, using an index on (created_at DESC, id DESC). If limit+1 rows come back, return nextCursor = base64(json(last.created_at, last.id)), otherwise null.

problems.title: Reliable webhook sender
problems.prompt: Design webhook delivery that never loses events and does not hammer failing consumers.
problems.solution: Write the outbox row in the same transaction as the state change. A worker sends signed POSTs with a 10 s timeout and retries on 5xx or timeout with exponential backoff and jitter for up to 3 days. After that, mark the endpoint as failing and notify the owner. Expose GET /events for replay, and keep per-endpoint concurrency limits.
